spec.notes: Primary variant is J=6/K=6 Panel A (no skip week), the strategy examined in most detail per the paper. The paper also reports a 16-strategy grid (J,K ∈ {3,6,9,12} months) with and without a 1-week skip (Panel B). Monthly returns are compounded from CRSP daily returns. Overlapping portfolios are used: each month holds K cohorts simultaneously. The 6/6 strategy is rebalanced monthly with equal weights maintained. [Engine post-fix: universe.min_price set to 10 (filters penny stocks). The paper's true window (1965-1989) is preserved on the spec; the engine runs on a 2007-2026 OOS window per the ENGINE_WINDOW_OVERRIDES table in app/main.py — that captures the post-2009-crash momentum revival without misrepresenting the paper. The KF factor-comparison banner independently validates the original 1965-1989 claim.]

criticisms.description: The spec silently hard-codes `universe.min_price = 10.0` with no textual basis in the paper. The paper's sole inclusion criterion is data availability: 'All stocks with available returns data in the J months preceding the portfolio formation date are included.' No price floor is mentioned anywhere. A $10 filter would disproportionately exclude small, low-priced stocks that drive the strongest momentum returns in the paper's size subsamples (S1). This is not flagged as an AmbiguityFlag; it is imposed as a spec value while the notes only parenthetically call it a penny-stock filter.

evidence_quote.text: All stocks with available returns data in the J months preceding the portfolio formation date are included in the sample from which the buy and sell portfolios are constructed.

criticisms.proposed_remediation: Remove `universe.min_price = 10.0` from the spec and add an AmbiguityFlag for `universe.min_price` at high severity with `default_chosen='none'` and alternatives `['1.00','5.00']`, noting the paper imposes no price floor.

criticisms.description: The spec collapses the paper's full 32-strategy grid (J,K ∈ {3,6,9,12} × Panel A/B) to a single J=6/K=6 Panel A variant, without flagging J=12/K=3 as the paper's stated most profitable strategy at 1.31%/month Panel A and 1.49%/month Panel B—roughly 38-57% higher than J=6/K=6. The spec notes acknowledge the grid exists but do not model J/K as ranges or surface J=12/K=3 as a high-priority alternative. A replicator following only the spec would miss the paper's headline maximum-return combination.

evidence_quote.text: The most successful zero-cost strategy selects stocks based on their returns over the previous 12 months and then holds the portfolio for 3 months. This strategy yields 1.31% per month (shown in Panel A)

criticisms.proposed_remediation: Add AmbiguityFlags at high severity for `signal.lookback_months` and `rebalance.holding_period_months` enumerating the full (J,K) grid and explicitly identifying J=12/K=3 as the paper's stated maximum-return alternative.

criticisms.description: The spec's rebalance fields do not capture the overlapping-cohort 1/K fractional weighting rule. The paper states the strategy 'revise[s] the weights on 1/K of the securities in the entire portfolio in any given month.' A naive reading of `holding_period_months=6` with `frequency=monthly` could be implemented as a single non-overlapping portfolio, producing materially different return series from the correctly overlapping composite. This implementation distinction is not surfaced as an AmbiguityFlag despite being critical to reproducing the paper's monthly return calculations.

evidence_quote.text: in any given month t, the strategies hold a series of portfolios that are selected in the current month as well as in the previous K - 1 months, where K is the holding period.

criticisms.proposed_remediation: Add an AmbiguityFlag at medium severity for `rebalance.overlapping_cohort_construction` documenting the 1/K monthly weight revision rule and flagging that a non-overlapping implementation would produce a materially different return series.

judgment.implementable_alpha_basis: cost_10bps row (0.958%/mo, t=1.84) at the default 10 bps round-trip; T+1 lag is already implicit in the monthly engine and skip_1m would actually improve to 1.23%/mo, so 10 bps remains the binding friction.
primary_failure_modes: First-half sample failure: subperiod_first_half (-0.69%/mo, t=-1.15) and subperiod_pre_2010 (-1.64%/mo, t=-1.07) — strategy did not work in the 2007-2016 era.
Crisis fragility: subperiod_gfc_2008_2009 (-2.57%/mo, t=-1.31) and subperiod_momentum_crash_2009 (-3.16%/mo, t=-1.02) — large negative returns in stress regimes.
Cost ceiling: alpha t-stat falls below 2 at 10 bps (cost_10bps t=1.84) and the strategy fails outright at cost_50bps (0.69%/mo, t=1.33).
judgment.gap_attribution_evidence: subperiod_first_half (-0.69%/mo, t=-1.15) and subperiod_first_third (-0.78%/mo, t=-0.92) fail while subperiod_second_half (2.79%/mo, t=4.56) and subperiod_last_third (3.62%/mo, t=4.60) carry the entire baseline — the temporal pattern is opposite of what survivorship-driven data_limitation would produce (survivorship bias usually inflates EARLY returns). Cost sweep survives through 25 bps, so the gap is not pure methodology fragility either; the dominant signature is regime concentration in the post-2016 window.
judgment.summary:
Implementable alpha is ~0.96%/mo (t=1.84) at 10 bps round-trip costs (cost_10bps), only marginally below the 1.02%/mo baseline; the strategy survives 16 of 26 stress tests and all swept cost levels through 25 bps, with capacity ~$17.4B at a 50 bps impact target. The lag sweep shows alpha actually strengthens at skip_1m through skip_6m (t=2.42-2.62), arguing this is a structural (not microstructure) signal.

The headline fragility is temporal concentration. subperiod_first_half (-0.69%/mo, t=-1.15), subperiod_first_third (-0.78%/mo, t=-0.92), and subperiod_pre_2010 (-1.64%/mo, t=-1.07) all sign-flip, while subperiod_second_half (2.79%/mo, t=4.56) and subperiod_last_third (3.62%/mo, t=4.60) carry the full 2007-2026 record. Crisis windows are catastrophic: GFC -2.57%/mo, the 2009 momentum crash -3.16%/mo, COVID -0.38%/mo. This is the post_publication_decay signature inverted in time — the strategy did not exist pre-2016 and only emerged in the recent regime; survivorship bias (the only flagged data limitation, with pit_vs_latest_universe NOT RUN) cannot explain why EARLY returns are weak. A discretionary PM should size this as a recent-regime bet, not a 20-year structural alpha, and demand a crisis-regime hedge before deployment. Confidence is medium: 6 families ran and ≥3 tests support each conclusion, but survivorship remains unquantified.

diagnosis.primary_cause_summary: Baseline already matched the paper (gap 0.075%/mo, verdict=match); D2 was invoked despite no real divergence, and the residual is attributable to OOS sample window and survivorship effects rather than a spec defect.
diagnosis.primary_cause_evidence: The baseline produced mean_return=0.01025 vs claimed 0.0095 (absolute_gap=0.00075, verdict=match) with sign already correct. Mutation #1 (signal.skip_months 0→1) widened the gap to 0.00280 and flipped verdict match→diverged, confirming Panel A's no-skip convention is the correct configuration. Mutation #2 reverted skip_months to 0 and restored the matching state (gap=0.00075, verdict=match), triggering early exit on tolerance.

proposal.rationale: Baseline already matches the paper (mean 1.025%/mo vs claimed 0.95%/mo, gap ~0.075%/mo, verdict="match"). The lower t-stat (1.97 vs 3.07) reflects the OOS 2007-2026 window (231 obs vs paper's 300) and post-2009 momentum volatility, not a spec defect. With no sign flip and gap < 2× tolerance, the loop should halt. The most informative remaining probe is signal.skip_months=1 — Panel B's 1-month skip is the canonical post-1993 momentum convention, typically adding 10-20 bps/mo by avoiding short-term reversal. This sensitivity test reveals whether the small residual gap widens (engine hotter than paper) or shrinks, providing useful diagnostic info on which panel the engine more closely tracks.

proposal.rationale: Experiment #1 mutated signal.skip_months 0→1 and widened the gap from 0.00075 to 0.00280 (verdict match→diverged), confirming that Panel A (no skip) is the correct configuration and the baseline already matches the paper within tolerance. The remaining residual (~0.075%/mo, well under 2× tolerance) is attributable to the OOS 2007-2026 window and survivorship bias flagged in data_quality_flags, not a spec defect. The right action is to revert skip_months to 0 (the baseline match state) so the loop halts on a matching configuration. With sign correct and gap < 2× tolerance, no further mutation is needed; this proposal restores the best-known state.

diagnosis.residual_gap_likely_cause: D2 was invoked even though the baseline verdict was already "match" with an absolute gap of 7.5 bps/mo — well within tolerance and with the correct sign. The remaining residual is best explained by sample-window differences rather than a spec defect: the engine runs an OOS 2007-2026 window (~231 monthly obs) versus the paper's 1965-1989 window (~300 obs), which also explains the t-stat shortfall (1.97 vs 3.07) since post-2009 momentum has exhibited higher volatility and a known crash episode (2009). Survivorship bias in the modern CRSP sample (flagged in data_quality_flags) is also consistent with the engine's slightly hotter mean return. The skip_months=1 sensitivity probe widening the gap confirms Panel A (no skip) is the correct configuration, ruling out signal-construction error.
diagnosis.early_exit_reason: gap within tolerance on experiment 2: |gap|=0.0007; baseline already matched and the sensitivity probe confirmed Panel A configuration is correct.
